\begin{abstract}
We study the convergence of gradient descent on smooth convex functions
and report experiments on two data sets.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}\label{sec:intro}
Optimization is at the heart of machine learning.\footnote{See the survey by Bottou et al.}
Given $f\colon \R^n \to \R$, we look for $x^\star = \arg\min_x f(x)$.

\section{Method}\label{sec:method}
The update rule is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:update}
  x_{k+1} = x_k - \eta \nabla f(x_k),
\end{equation}
where $\eta > 0$ is the step size. Equation~\eqref{eq:update} converges when
$\eta \leq \frac{1}{L}$ and
\begin{align}
  f(x_{k+1}) &\leq f(x_k) - \frac{\eta}{2}\norm{\nabla f(x_k)}^2 \\
  \sum_{i=1}^{n} \alpha_i^2 &\approx \sqrt{2} \nonumber
\end{align}
